title: Linkability of homeowner identity to enrolled devices
description: During account registration and device enrollment, the homeowner's identity becomes linked to their cameras and sensors. This creates a persistent link that could enable tracking of the homeowner's activities across devices or over time.
assumptions: Homeowner provides identifying information during registration

title: Identifiability of homeowner during registration
description: The registration process requires the homeowner to provide account credentials and personal information, making them directly identifiable within the Home Hub system.
assumptions: Registration requires personal identifying information

title: Disclosure of sensitive registration data
description: Account credentials, device information, and personal data transmitted during registration could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission from Homeowner to Home Hub.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network connection

title: Unawareness of data collection scope
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of what data is collected during registration, how it will be used, stored, or shared with third parties beyond the immediate enrollment process.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not be fully understood or disclosed

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: The registration and enrollment process may not fully comply with privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.) regarding consent, data minimization, transparency, or purpose limitation.
assumptions: System may not implement all regulatory requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific implementation and jurisdiction

title: Guest presence detectable through door unlock activity
description: An observer could detect that a guest is present at the property by observing the door unlock event triggered by the access code entry. This reveals the guest's participation in the system without requiring access to the actual data.
assumptions: The Home Hub logs or emits observable signals when the door is unlocked

title: Temporary access code disclosure during transmission
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest could be intercepted or disclosed during transmission to the Home Hub, potentially allowing unauthorized parties to gain access to the property.
assumptions: The access code is transmitted in a way that could be intercepted (e.g., wireless, network)

title: Guest unaware of data collection scope
description: The guest may not be aware that their access patterns, timing, and usage metadata are being collected and stored by the Home Hub beyond just the door unlock function.
assumptions: The system collects metadata about access attempts without explicit guest notification

title: Linkability of guest identity to access patterns
description: The temporary access code usage could be linked to specific guest identities through system logs, enabling correlation of access patterns with individual guests over time.
assumptions: The system maintains logs that associate access codes with guest identities or profiles
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether the system actually links temporary codes to guest identities

title: Event Linkability to Individuals
description: Motion, door, and sensor events written to the local log could be linked to specific individuals based on timing, location, and patterns of activity within the home.
assumptions: The event log contains sufficient contextual data (timestamps, sensor IDs) to enable correlation with individual behavior.

title: Individual Identifiability from Event Patterns
description: Aggregated event data in the local log could enable identification of specific individuals through behavioral patterns, occupancy schedules, and movement patterns.
assumptions: Event data includes sufficient granularity (time, location) to support individual identification when analyzed.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Event Log Data
description: The local event log containing motion/door/sensor events could be accessed by unauthorized parties, revealing sensitive information about home occupancy and activity patterns.
assumptions: The local event log may not have adequate access controls or encryption at rest.

title: Data Aggregation Revealing Behavioral Patterns
description: Multiple sensor events aggregated in the local log over time could reveal detailed behavioral patterns, daily routines, and occupancy schedules of home residents.
assumptions: Event data is retained long enough and with sufficient detail to enable pattern analysis.

title: User Unawareness of Event Logging
description: Home users may be unaware of what sensor events are being logged, how long they are retained, or what inferences can be drawn from the event data.
assumptions: Privacy notices or user interfaces may not clearly communicate logging practices.

title: Lack of User Control Over Event Data
description: Users may have limited or no control over what events are logged, how long they are retained, or the ability to delete or export their event data.
assumptions: The system may not provide user-facing controls for event log management.

title: Unauthorized access to cloud-stored video clips
description: Video clips stored in cloud video storage (DS2) could be accessed by unauthorized parties through cloud service breaches, compromised credentials, or insider threats, exposing sensitive home surveillance footage.
assumptions: Cloud storage provider has security controls but may be vulnerable to attacks

title: Identifiable individuals in video footage
description: Video clips uploaded to cloud storage may contain identifiable individuals (residents, visitors, neighbors), enabling identification and potential tracking of people captured by home cameras.
assumptions: Camera clips contain visual data of people

title: Aggregation of video clips for behavioral profiling
description: Multiple video clips stored over time in cloud storage could be aggregated to create detailed behavioral profiles, movement patterns, and activity schedules of household members.
assumptions: Video clips are stored with timestamps and can be correlated

title: Linkability of video data to specific home/user
description: Video clips uploaded from the home hub could be linked to a specific household or user identity through metadata, account associations, or device identifiers in the cloud storage system.
assumptions: Cloud storage maintains user/device associations with uploaded content

title: User unawareness of data upload scope
description: Home users may be unaware of the extent of video data being uploaded to cloud storage, including what is recorded, how long it's retained, and who has access to it.
assumptions: Users may not fully understand cloud storage implications

title: Potential non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Storing video surveillance footage in cloud storage may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent, data minimization, or retention policies are not implemented.
assumptions: Applicable privacy regulations exist for video surveillance data
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and specific implementation

title: Motion alert data excessively exposed to backend
description: The Home Hub forwards real-time motion alerts to the Mobile App Backend. This transfer may expose more personal data than necessary (e.g., precise timing, frequency, and location of motion events) beyond what is strictly required for the alert functionality. The data could reveal occupancy patterns, daily routines, and presence/absence of individuals in the home.
assumptions: Motion alerts contain timestamped location data that could be used to infer occupancy patterns and personal routines.

title: Motion data reveals occupancy and behavioral patterns
description: The motion alert transmitted from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend may disclose information about when individuals are present or absent from the home, their movement patterns, and daily routines. This information could be used to infer sensitive personal details about the household.
assumptions: Motion detection data includes sufficient granularity to infer occupancy and behavioral patterns.

title: Motion alerts linkable to specific individuals or households
description: Motion alert data transmitted to the backend could be linked to specific individuals or households, especially when combined with other data sources. This linkability could enable profiling or tracking of individuals' presence and movement patterns.
assumptions: The motion alert data contains identifiers or can be correlated with other data to identify specific individuals or households.

title: Motion detection data aggregation
description: Multiple motion-detected notifications over time can be aggregated to build a detailed profile of the homeowner's presence patterns, daily routines, and occupancy habits, revealing sensitive behavioral information beyond the immediate notification purpose.
assumptions: Notifications are sent consistently over time and stored or logged by the system

title: Notification interception during transmission
description: Motion detection notifications could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission from the mobile app backend to the homeowner's phone, potentially revealing when motion was detected and at what times.
assumptions: Transmission occurs over network that could be vulnerable to interception

title: Homeowner unawareness of data collection scope
description: Homeowners may not be fully aware of what motion data is being collected, how frequently notifications are generated, or how this data could be used beyond the immediate notification purpose.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain motion detection data practices

title: Linkability of motion events to homeowner identity
description: Motion detection notifications can be linked to the specific homeowner's identity and potentially correlated with other data sources to build a comprehensive activity profile.
assumptions: Notifications are tied to specific user accounts and can be cross-referenced with other data

title: Linkability of aggregated analytics to individual users
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with the cloud analytics vendor could potentially be linked back to individual users through linkage attacks, especially if the vendor has access to other data sources or if aggregation granularity is insufficient.
assumptions: Vendor may have additional data sources; aggregation may not provide sufficient anonymization

title: Data misuse by cloud analytics vendor
description: The cloud analytics vendor may use the device-usage analytics for purposes beyond the agreed scope, such as selling to third parties, advertising targeting, or other commercial purposes not disclosed to users.
assumptions: Vendor has commercial incentives to monetize data; contractual controls may be insufficient

title: Unauthorized disclosure of analytics data
description: Analytics data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through security breaches at the vendor, insider threats, or interception during transmission from P2 to EE3.
assumptions: Vendor security controls may have vulnerabilities; data in transit may not be adequately protected

title: User unawareness of third-party data sharing
description: Mobile app users may not be aware that their device-usage analytics are being shared with a third-party cloud analytics vendor, or may not understand the extent and implications of this data sharing.
assumptions: Privacy notices may be unclear or buried; users may not read privacy policies

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: The data sharing arrangement may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.), or the vendor may fail to meet their compliance obligations as a data processor.
assumptions: Vendor compliance posture unknown; regulatory requirements may be complex
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific vendor agreements and jurisdiction

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video content during retrieval
description: Video clips retrieved from cloud storage to the mobile app backend could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission, exposing sensitive footage of the homeowner's property.
assumptions: Video data is transmitted over network between DS2 and P2

title: Identifiable information in retrieved video clips
description: Video clips may contain personally identifiable information such as faces, license plates, or property identifiers that could be exposed when retrieved by the backend process.
assumptions: Video footage contains visual data that can identify individuals or property

title: Linkability through video retrieval patterns
description: Patterns of video clip retrieval could be correlated to infer homeowner behavior, presence at home, or daily routines, enabling linkage of different data points about the user.
assumptions: Retrieval metadata (timestamps, frequency, clip IDs) is logged or observable

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video clips may be stored longer than necessary for the stated purpose of playback, or retrieved for purposes beyond what the homeowner consented to.
assumptions: Storage duration and retrieval purposes are not strictly controlled
uncertainty_note: Context Nc.1.1.4 from retrieved knowledge applies to storage limitation - applying to retrieval context with some uncertainty
